title: The bounded universal search is congruent in its predicate
statement: For all Boolean predicates f and g on the naturals and every bound n, if f and g agree at every index then the bounded searches `allBelow f n` and `allBelow g n` return the same Boolean.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Finset.allBelow_congr : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x3) (x1 x3))) -> Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.allBelow x0 x2) (AxNat.Finset.allBelow x1 x2)))))

notes: The law `Nat.Finset.allBelow` was missing, and a THIRD kind: its three existing laws (`allBelow_of_all_true`, `allBelow_true_at`, `allBelow_false_witness`) all relate a loop to its predicate's VALUES, and none relates two loops to each other. Measured absent before proving, at 3,222 declarations with a freshly built `shape_search`: `--const Nat.Finset.allBelow_congr` UNANSWERABLE against the positive control `--name-like allBelow` FOUND 4. It is what discharges `Nat.Finset.forallSubset_of_search`'s congruence premise for a bounded inclusion test, which is why Hall's sufficiency direction needed it. The proof is an induction on the bound with NO case split on the predicate's value -- unlike all three existing laws -- because two congruences close the successor case, one through the `then` branch and one through the scrutinee. ADR-1644.
